findings.scenario: A Ruby file defines a method named handler and then assigns handler = lambda { |x| target(x) } (or proc with a brace block). The call inside the closure is now attributed to the unrelated handler method, creating a false CALLS edge.
findings.evidence: The new patterns attach a Function definition named handler to the closure block, but RUBY_QUERIES in tree-sitter-queries.ts only emits closure Function nodes for assignment right: (lambda), not the (call) forms lambda/proc. A source-worker probe emitted only Method:a.rb:handler#1 and Method:a.rb:target#1 for this fixture. resolveDefGraphId therefore misses the closure position/qualified keys and aliases its definition through simpleKey to Method:a.rb:handler#1. Executing emitReferencesViaLookup with the new captures produced Method:a.rb:handler#1 -> Method:a.rb:target#1; removing only the newly added closure declaration capture restored File:a.rb -> Method:a.rb:target#1.
findings.recommendation: Add matching graph-node definition rules for the lambda/proc call forms alongside these scope declarations, and cover a binding that shares its name with an existing method so the closure cannot alias that method.
